entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf ibn Maṭar was a mathematician and translator of Persian and Greek works during the Abbasid Caliphate. Born in the 8th century, his contributions to algebra and trigonometry had a lasting impact on Islamic and European scholarship. His translations of ancient Greek texts, including Ptolemy's Almagest, influenced the development of astronomy in the Islamic Golden Age. The works of Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf ibn Maṭar were widely disseminated throughout the Middle East and Europe, shaping the intellectual landscape of the medieval period. His legacy can be seen in the work of later mathematicians and astronomers, such as Ibn Yunus and Ulugh Beg, who built upon his discoveries. The significance of Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf ibn Maṭar's contributions can be measured in the enduring impact of his translations on the development of astronomy and mathematics in the Islamic world and beyond.

entities.summary: Al-\u1e7ajj\u060c ibn Y\u062f ibn Ma\u060car (786 CE - 833 CE) was a mathematician and translator who played a crucial role in the transmission of ancient Greek knowledge to the Islamic world during the Abbasid Caliphate. His most notable works include the translation of Ptolemy's Almagest and the compilation of the book \u0627\u0628\u0621\u062f\u0647\u0627\u0628\u0629\u0644\u0627\u0644\u062f\u0627\u0628\u0628\u0629 (The Book of the Causes and Effects of Things). This translation had a profound impact on the development of Islamic astronomy and mathematics, influencing prominent scholars such as Al-Biruni and Ibn Yunus. Al-\u1e7ajj\u060c ibn Y\u062f ibn Ma\u060car's work also contributed to the spread of scientific knowledge throughout the Middle East and Europe, laying the groundwork for the Renaissance. His legacy extends beyond his mathematical contributions, as he played a key role in preserving and transmitting ancient Greek texts during a period of significant cultural and intellectual exchange.
